author: c2-sql-edu-critic (independent education critic subagent, fresh context, read-only; rechecked commit f18bccaf)

findings.claim: New in f18bccaf; C1/F5, wrong rule. The correction to C2E-SEED-04 added a caption rule: lead_id points at another instructor, "so within one INSERT a lead's row comes before the rows that point at it." The page's own editor contradicts it. Replayed: INSERT INTO instructors (instructor_id, name, lead_id) VALUES (2, 'Tomas', 1), (1, 'Mara', NULL); prints INSERT 0 2 and both rows. PostgreSQL also checks a non-deferrable foreign key after the whole command, not row by row (per the SET CONSTRAINTS reference, which the page already lists as a source); the SME critic should confirm that against live docs. A learner who reads the rule and then sees the editor accept the opposite order gets two conflicting answers.
findings.recommendation: Drop the "within one INSERT" clause. Keep "lead_id points at another instructor, the person's team lead". If ordering inside one statement matters to the lesson, say it accurately, for example "the key is checked when the whole INSERT finishes, so rows inside one INSERT may come in any order".
